provenance.instrument: Concord Township (Delaware County) Code Chapter 210 Zoning (Ord. No. 132, 12-7-1982, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 code date 2025-05-13 (breadcrumb). New Laws on 2026-11-14: Ord. No. 412 (2025-12-02), budget, not zoning.
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 breadcrumb 'Code 2025-05-13'. The only New Law (Ord. No. 412, budget) is not zoning.
checks: The zoning code has no general accessory dwelling unit rule. Each residential district allows the listed uses 'and for no other' (210-10, 210-18, 210-26, 210-34, 210-40.2). A single-family detached dwelling is 'occupied exclusively as a residence for only one family' (210-4)

Historic path: on a property with a Class I or Class II historic resource on the Historic Resources Map, 'An additional dwelling unit, over and above existing zoning requirements, may be allowed' by conditional use: Township Council approval after a hearing, with a historic resource study and Historical Commission review (210-183.7A, B). A property too small for two dwelling units under the district rules is barred on this path. The relief is a Zoning Hearing Board variance of lot size, lot dimension or yards for a Class I or Class II historic resource (210-183.8A)

The historic added unit has no more than two bedrooms, is 'totally contained within the historic resource' (in the historic house or wholly in the historic barn or outbuilding), has rear or side parking for two more vehicles, and the property must be large enough for two dwelling units under the district rules (210-183.7B)

R-PRD-1 planned residential development: 'Single-family residence with an accessory apartment' is a permitted use (210-72A(1)(f)) only in a planned residential development of 50 acres or more in one ownership with public water and sewer (210-71), and only on a lot the approved development plan designates for that housing type. The housing mix is subject to Township Council approval (210-72A(1)), and these houses are at most 30% of the development's units at no more than 5 units per net acre (210-74C(8)). Another lot needs a Council plan amendment. The apartment is attached, 600 to 1,000 sq ft, at most two bedrooms, on a lot deed restricted against division (210-4, 210-74C(17)). Its yards may be varied by the Township Council or the review agency (210-74C(4), (13))

Garage heights differ from the 15 ft accessory cap (210-292B 'other than as permitted in § 210-293'): a private garage wider than 18 ft may be up to 18 ft, one story with a loft of at most 30% of its floor (210-293D(2)), on a property over three acres a garage may be 18 ft (210-293G), and no garage may be taller than the house (210-293D(3)). A detached garage is at most 50% of the house's first floor area (210-293F) and may not be used for 'overnight accommodations or sleeping quarters' (210-293J)
Concordville Village Overlay design guidelines (Article XIII) apply to development in R-2 and R-3 (210-18, 210-34, 210-36)

Accessory buildings in residential districts: at most one story or the height of the house and never over 15 ft; at most 750 sq ft and one detached accessory building on a property under three acres; all accessory buildings together at most 75% of the house's first floor area; not in the front yard and at least 10 ft behind the rearmost part of the house; over 250 sq ft within the principal building setbacks. A detached garage may not be used for 'overnight accommodations or sleeping quarters' and may have no full bathroom or kitchen equipment (210-292, 210-293)

R-3 lot and yard figures depend on whether the development plan was approved before or after May 11, 1959 (210-35A, B). The yards shown are the later figures. A historic R-3 lot needs 30,000 sq ft for two units on an earlier plan and 60,000 sq ft on a later one

R-1 cluster development (210-12): lots of 21,780 sq ft, 16 ft side and rear yards, 20 ft from the right-of-way, 20% building area, accessory buildings one story. The R-1 row holds the conventional figures
Parking: 2 spaces per dwelling unit for a single-family dwelling (210-197G)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Concord Township (Delaware County) Zoning Officer. eCode360 code CO1622 is Concord Township, Delaware County (Bethel Road, Baltimore Pike, Concord Mills, Concordville). Read on eCode360 in a browser, one page at a time, on 2026-11-14 (a first author read the definitions of accessory apartment, 210-72, 210-74 and 210-183.7 the same day; this author read 210-183.7 and 210-74C(17) again). Code search (all content, New Laws included) for 'accessory apartment', 'accessory dwelling', 'living quarters', 'immediate family', 'in-law', ECHO, 'elder cottage', granny, 'family dwelling', relative, 'housekeeping unit', conversion, 'two-family', duplex, caretaker, 'tenant house', 'guest house' and 'accessory living' found the accessory apartment definitions and 210-72 (R-PRD-1), caretaker quarters in R-A (210-42) and R-PLO (210-171), conversion to professional office in M/I (210-225), and the Historic Resources Inventory (a PDF attachment, not opened). Read in full: Articles III, IV, V, VI, VIA, XXII, XXV, XXXV, 210-183.7, 210-183.8, and 210-4 up to the I entries. District codes from 210-5 and 210-290 (R-PRD-1). Not ADUs, noted only: living accommodation for a proprietor, watchman or caretaker or live-work units, not on the first floor, in C-1 and C-2 (210-119, 210-127), caretaker quarters in R-A (210-42), R-PLO (210-171) and LI (210-152), as cited by a reviewer and not read here. Not read: R-A, R-AH, R-MHD, R-PRD-2, R-PRD-3, C-1, C-2, M/I, LI, PIP, R-PLO, PBPD use lists, the Concordville Village Overlay (210-125.1), Article XXVII conditional use standards, Article XXXII open space, the rest of Article X from 210-75 (210-78 to 210-82 approval procedure), the remaining definitions (J to Z), and the PDF attachments (Historic Resources Map and Inventory, Zoning Map).

term.value: accessory apartment (planned residential development) and additional dwelling unit (historic resource)
term.note: 210-4: 'DWELLING, SINGLE-FAMILY RESIDENCE WITH AN ACCESSORY APARTMENT A detached single-family residential unit with an attached apartment, the total area of such apartment not to exceed 1,000 square feet ... constituting two dwelling units on a single lot.' Listed only in R-PRD-1. A historic resource may get 'An additional dwelling unit' by conditional use (210-183.7B).

status.note: No general ADU rule. The residence districts allow the listed uses 'and for no other', and none lists an accessory apartment. The accessory apartment is listed only inside an R-PRD-1 planned residential development, and an added unit is open only in a Class I or Class II historic resource by conditional use (210-183.7).

path.note: 'A building may be erected, altered or used ... for any of the purposes set forth in this section and for no other.' A second unit on a house lot that is not in a historic resource or an R-PRD-1 development needs a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board.

fallback_path.note: Relief from a district rule is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board. For a historic resource the Board may vary lot size, lot dimension or yards when needed to preserve the resource (210-183.8A).

historic_path.note: 'An additional dwelling unit, over and above existing zoning requirements, may be allowed in a historic dwelling, barn, outbuilding or other building' that is a Class I or Class II historic resource, after a historic resource study, Historical Commission review and 'Approval of the Township Council following a conditional use hearing'. No family or owner rule. Conditions in gates.

value.term: single-family residence with an accessory apartment
value.note: A permitted use within an R-PRD-1 planned residential development, on a lot the approved development plan designates as a single-family residence with an accessory apartment. With that designation it is by right. Otherwise the plan must be amended with Township Council approval (210-70, 210-72A(1)). The apartment is attached, 600 to 1,000 sq ft, at most two bedrooms.

district_paths.note: District code R-PRD-1 as listed in 210-5 and 210-290. The eCode360 article title reads 'XR-PRD-1'. The R-PRD-1 sections other than 210-68 to 210-74 were not read (210-75 onward, the approval procedure).

zoning_districts.note: No residence district lists a general ADU. R-PRD-1 has its own district path (approval.district_paths). The historic path follows the Historic Resources Map, not a district.

building_types.note: Not limited by a town-wide rule. 210-183.7 does not limit the historic dwelling to a detached house: the unit is in a historic dwelling, barn or outbuilding. The R-PRD-1 apartment needs a detached house (gate). The residence districts R-1 to R-4 permit single-family detached dwellings only.

historic_bypass.note: A Class I or Class II historic resource may get an added dwelling unit by conditional use. Confirm the class on the Historic Resources Map (a PDF attachment).

historic_test.value: The property has a Class I or Class II historic resource on the Concord Township Historic Resources Map
historic_test.note: 'each Class I or Class II historic resource dwelling, barn, outbuilding or other building as defined on the Historic Resources Map'.

value.condition: The attached accessory apartment is listed only in an R-PRD-1 planned residential development (210-72A(1)(f)). Every other district allows its listed uses 'and for no other'.

The lot is designated on the approved R-PRD-1 development plan as a 'single-family residence with an accessory apartment'. Being in an approved planned residential development is not enough: the housing mix is 'subject to the approval of the Township Council' (210-72A(1)), these houses are at most 30% of the development's units (210-74C(8)(c)[5]) at no more than 5 units per net acre in their areas (210-74C(8)(a)[5]). A lot shown for another housing type needs a plan amendment approved by Township Council.
The R-PRD-1 accessory apartment is attached to 'a detached single-family residential unit' (210-4). A twin or townhouse in the development does not qualify.
The planned residential development is at least 50 acres in one ownership.
The development is served by public sewer.
The development is served by public water.
The apartment is 600 to 1,000 sq ft with at most two bedrooms. The lot is held in title by one owner and deed restricted against further division.

The building is a Class I or Class II historic resource (dwelling, barn, outbuilding or other building) on the Historic Resources Map. A historic resource study (210-183.10), Historical Commission review and recommendation, and Township Council approval after a conditional use hearing.

'The dwelling unit shall be totally contained within the historic resource': an apartment in the historic house, or wholly inside the historic barn, outbuilding or other building. No more than two bedrooms.

The property is 'of sufficient size to comply with the zoning requirements of the district for two dwelling units': the added unit counts. 87,120 sq ft in R-1, R-2 and R-2D (43,560 per family), 30,000 in R-4 (15,000 per family), in R-3 30,000 on a plan approved before May 11, 1959 and 60,000 on a later plan. A smaller property is barred on this path. The relief is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board, which may modify lot size, lot dimension or yard requirements for plans affecting Class I and Class II historic resources when needed to preserve the resource (210-183.8A).

R-3 on a development plan approved after May 11, 1959: the property needs 60,000 sq ft for the house and the added unit (30,000 sq ft per family, 210-35B(1)). The tool tests the earlier plans' 30,000 sq ft. Ask the zoning officer which plan applies. Below 60,000 sq ft on a later plan the relief is a variance (210-183.8A).

In a cluster development the minimum lot area of specific lots may be lowered to as low as a quarter acre and averaged with others to give the historic resource more land. The lot and yard figures of a historic resource and the lots next to it may be adjusted, if no alternatives exist, to keep the resource on its own lot.

Additions or alterations to the historic structure and all landscaping conform to the zoning and subdivision and land development rules and follow the Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation as closely as possible.

types_allowed.note: Off the historic path only the R-PRD-1 accessory apartment, 'a detached single-family residential unit with an attached apartment' (210-4). It is barred outside R-PRD-1 (gate). The historic path forms are in form.types_allowed_historic.

types_allowed_historic.note: 'The dwelling unit may be in the form of an apartment unit in the historic dwelling or may be wholly contained within the barn, outbuilding or other building.' It is 'totally contained within the historic resource', so an addition or a new building is not this path.

value.garage_conversion: Unit wholly inside a historic barn or outbuilding

max_sqft.note: No floor area cap for the historic unit. At most two bedrooms (210-183.7B(1)). The R-PRD-1 accessory apartment is 600 to 1,000 sq ft (210-74C(17)).

front_yard_barred.note: 'No accessory building or structure shall be erected or placed within a front yard', and it stands at least 10 ft farther back from the front street line than the rearmost part of the house, attached decks included.

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'A detached private garage or other detached accessory building greater than 250 square feet in area shall be located within the setbacks of the principal permitted building.' Older text allows 5 ft from side and rear lines (210-222B, C).

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 'No accessory building or structure of any kind, other than as permitted in § 210-293, shall exceed one story or the height of the existing residence, and in no event be greater than 15 feet high.' Garages differ: a private garage wider than 18 ft may be up to 18 ft with a loft (210-293D(2)), and 18 ft on a property over three acres (210-293G). A detached garage may not hold sleeping quarters (210-293J), so the garage figures do not reach a dwelling unit.

accessory_structure_max_sqft.note: 'No accessory building on a property of less than three acres shall exceed 750 square feet in area.' All accessory buildings together at most 75% of the house's first floor area (210-292G).

accessory_cap_binds_adu.note: The historic unit sits in an existing historic barn or outbuilding. Additions and alterations must conform to zoning (210-183.7B(3)), but whether the accessory size and height caps reach an existing historic building is not said.

height_capped_at_house.note: Not taller than the existing residence.

owner_occupancy.note: No owner rule for the historic added unit.

family_only.note: No family rule for the historic added unit.

spaces_required.note: 'Sufficient off-street parking, to the rear or side, to accommodate two additional vehicles'.

total_on_site.note: Single-family dwelling '2 per dwelling unit' for the house plus two for the added unit.

adu_max_sqft.note: 'A minimum of 600 square feet and a maximum of 1,000 square feet.'

setback_front_ft.note: For a single-family residence with an accessory apartment. The Township Council may require other setbacks and building distances (210-74C(4)) and the review agency may vary these requirements (210-74C(13)).

setback_side_ft.note: Minimum side yard 15 ft, aggregate 40 ft.

parking_spaces.note: 'Each dwelling unit must have space to park two automobiles off the street' (210-74G(1)). 4 in total for the house and the apartment.

min_lot_sqft.note: 'A lot area not less than one acre, 43,560 square feet, per family' (210-11A(1)). Width 150 ft at the building line.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: 'Per family' for every building used in whole or in part as a dwelling. The historic added unit needs a property 'of sufficient size to comply with the zoning requirements of the district for two dwelling units' (210-183.7B(5)), so 87,120 sq ft. Below that the relief is a variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (210-183.8A).

setback_front_ft.note: From each street right-of-way on which the lot abuts.

setback_side_ft.note: 'Side yards, either side: 20 feet; total of 50 feet for both.'

setback_sides_total_ft.note: Both side yards together 50 ft, at least 20 ft each.

principal_max_height_ft.note: 'The maximum height of buildings and other structures shall be 35 feet' (210-11B).

max_building_coverage.note: 'The building area shall not exceed 25% of the lot area.' Building area is the footprint of the buildings on the lot (210-4).

min_lot_sqft.note: 'A lot area not less than one acre, 43,560 square feet, per family' (210-11A(1)). Width 150 ft at the building line. R-2 uses the R-1 figures (210-19).

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family dwelling on a development plan approved after May 11, 1959: 30,000 sq ft per family, width 100 ft. On a plan approved before May 11, 1959: 15,000 sq ft per family, width 75 ft, front 30 ft, side 15 ft (30 ft both), rear 25 ft (210-35A). The row holds the later figures. Ask which applies to the lot.

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: The lower of the two R-3 figures. 'Not less than 15,000 square feet per family' on a development plan approved before May 11, 1959 (210-35A(1)), 30,000 sq ft per family on a plan approved after it (210-35B(1)). A historic lot needs room for two units: at least 30,000 sq ft on the earlier plans and 60,000 sq ft on the later ones. Below that the relief is a variance (210-183.8A).

setback_front_ft.note: 30 ft on a plan approved before May 11, 1959.

setback_side_ft.note: 'Side yards, either side: 25 feet; total of 50 feet for both.' Before May 11, 1959: 15 ft, 30 ft for both.

setback_sides_total_ft.note: 30 ft on a plan approved before May 11, 1959.

setback_rear_ft.note: 25 ft on a plan approved before May 11, 1959.

principal_max_height_ft.note: Article VI gives no height. Not settled whether the R-1 35 ft applies (210-35C points to R-1 only for other permitted uses).

max_building_coverage.note: 'The building area shall not exceed 25% of the lot area.'

min_lot_sqft.note: 'Not less than 15,000 square feet per family'. Average 19,500 sq ft in the development, width 75 ft. R-4 is a lot averaging development of 50 acres or more with public water and sewer (210-40.3A).

lot_area_per_unit_sqft.note: Per family. Density at most 2.5 units per acre in the development (210-40.3B(1)(c)).

setback_side_ft.note: 'Side yards: either side 10 feet, total of 30 feet for both.'
